what: In a zero-gravity rapier world, 100 balls (radius 1, 30 on touch devices) spawn scattered in a 5-cell box at the center, and every frame an impulse of (normalized own position)×(-.2,-.4,-.2) gathers them to the center — pulled twice as hard vertically, giving a horizontally wide cloud (movement damping .75 · rotation damping .15 · bounce .8). The z that the cursor points at=Kinematic balls (radius 1) invisible at the 0 plane position are moved directly to push through the cloud, and every 1 second one ball is thrown back to the rear top (z -3.5~-2.5) so the cloud keeps churning. The balls glow in a color one tone darker than the background, and top and bottom spotlights (intensity 60) make a faint shadow (VSM) where they meet. data-fx-part="text" If present, that text is broken per character onto the back panel and drawn large (70% of the width at 18 characters), and made to undulate on a 36-second cycle with large-cell value noise. options.measure-tall: Text column width share on vertical screens, default .65
options.per-line: On landscape screens, how many character sizes the cell width is divided into (character size = Cell width ÷ this value, default 18

note: Ball color is --fx-ball (default color-mix(in srgb, --kf-ink 14%, --kf-bg)) — emitted with the same color so at exposure 1.2 it reads one tone darker than the background. Glyph shape and color are read from the computed style of the text child (font-family·font-weight·color), and that child is hidden on screen only once the canvas is up. The original moves the cursor ball only while the pointer moves (no lag) and it starts at the center (0,0,0), so the cloud wraps around it and clumps. The original physics step follows the frame interval as is, but here it is clamped to 1/240~1/30 s. rapier is 2MB so it loads separately on attach (after three-global.js → three.cjs), and if it fails to load the cloud only glides over 2s into a flat ellipsoid spot. With reduced motion it stands there at once. pile-gather-push, which pushes the same rapier pile, is a different feel — it pulls ten model shapes proportionally by position and follows the cursor with lag

what: Photo panels are joined in a single line (horizontal or vertical) and flow endlessly with wheel or drag inside a perspective-tilted cluster (WebGL). what: A single character image (img or inline SVG) is put into WebGL as a 48×40 grid mesh, and each bone (axis → tip, radius r) swings its limb by ± an angle on a 1.6s cycle of (0.5 − 0.5cos). name: card-trail-loop

what: A grid tiled endlessly by one shader from a bundle of photo cards — 3 cards on the short side, 2px gap between cards. It flows right on its own by .003 cards per frame, and when dragged (mouse 1px = .002 per step, touch .005) on release, then each frame it slides with decay .95 (the wheel adds delta × .0002 to velocity). The faster it moves, the wider the gaps open (velocity × 20 chased in .1 steps, max 9% of the card), and the edges bend inward like a tunnel pulled toward the center, darkening by .2 (velocity × 15 in .08 steps). On first open it is bulged like a fisheye (lens: 1) until fx:release flattens it.

name: char-glint-title

what: Splits one line of text into characters and applies one of ten glitch types (look), redrawing every 2 to 3 frames at a 60fps frame basis, scaled by intensity. Block: a random color plate on 1/3 of characters breathes from 0 to 1x, with dotted, double or dashed borders of 0.1 to 0.5em and corners from 0 to 100%. Blur: 1/4 of characters are split into top and bottom halves, one half is blurred 0 to 20px and pushed up to 20% of the character width. Echo: 1/3 of characters are duplicated 4 to 8 times, rotated on a radius of 45% of the character size and scaled down by 1.5/n to 3.5/n. Strike: a strikethrough of 0 to 1em thickness across the whole line, switching between dotted, solid and wavy. Wave: 1/4 of characters are cut into 10 vertical strips, each shifting up and down by 20% on a sin wave. Font: each character gets a random decorative typeface, an inverted black-and-white plate, italics and a .4 to 1em size, every 10 to 30 frames. Slice: 1/4 of characters are cut into 20 horizontal strips, each offset left or right by 20 to 50%. Scale: every third character spreads 8 copies at 1 to 2x, ±90° and ±20px. Wobble: the whole line tilts and wobbles in 3D by ±50° or twists by ±20°. Shadow: characters are emptied to the background color and three ink-black shadow layers at 45° and 135° sway with an 11px gap. At intensity 0 the original text shows unchanged. Every frame there is a 1% chance of switching the branch within the type.

options.rate: Intensity. Default chaos (--fx-chaos, 1 if absent) · number (fixed)

name: char-reel-swap

what: Letters are stacked in two vertical sets, and on hover they roll up one line so the second set rises — with a per-letter delay (default .03s) one letter at a time, with 0 the whole word rolls. A faint first set → bold second set swap is also possible. Current page link (aria-current=page) stops where it rolled

options.stagger: Delay between characters (sec), default .03 — 0 means whole word
options.tone: With ”dim” the first set is --kf-dim and the second set is --kf-ink · with ”ink” the first set keeps the inherited color and only the second set is --kf-ink (beige text turning white, Brand A) · with ”under” the first set keeps the inherited color and only the second set rising from below is --kf-dim (the gray shadow copy of Brand B)
options.mode: With ‹once›, each time the pointer comes over it the whole word rolls once (ignoring delay) and the second layer rises, then returns to its place. It does not roll back when the pointer leaves, and it rolls again only after another hover (Brand A: dur .75 · ease 0.19,1,0.22,1 · gap 2). With ‹hold›, the enter plays through for hold seconds before the leave is accepted, and the leave returns to place at once with no curve. If the pointer returns in between, it carries on from there (Brand B: stagger .02 · dur 1.2 · ease 0,0.8,0.17,1 · hold .8).
options.gap: Gap between the two sets — a number is px, with a unit it is used as is (.4167vw), default 0. The second set sits below 100% + gap and rolls that much further (Site A mode: once 2 · Site B default form .4167vw) · in mode: hold too the first set rises to −(100% + gap) (Site C 20% — original first set −120% · clone 110%)
options.hold: Length in seconds that mode: hold keeps the entrance held, default .8 — original data-enter-time
options.back: If “end”, on leaving it reverses from the last letter (default is from the first letter, as on entering)
options.cut: In mode: once, cuts the roll at this many seconds and snaps back in place — if it comes back into view before the cut, it does not roll again. Default none (rolls to the end) (city site: dur 1 · ease 0.19,1,0.22,1 · cut .6)
options.skew: Roll the whole line at an angle (deg) — the line rolls as one piece, not letter by letter, the first copy leaves tilting by skewY around the bottom right, and the second comes up already tilted and straightens around the bottom left (century: skew: 32; stagger: 0; dur: .6; ease: 0.25,0.1,0.25,1 — CSS ease)
options.frames: mode: once — number of frames to wait before rolling, default 2 (two frames after the clone is attached) — 0 rolls as soon as the pointer touches, and re-entering while it is rolling does not start a new roll (original site)
options.lead: In mode: once, only the first set moves up and fades out over this many seconds (the second set rises in over dur) — no default (both sets roll together). Brand: lead .6 · lead-ease 0.25,0.46,0.45,0.94 · dur .4
options.lead-ease: lead’s curve is of the type ‹0.87,0,0.13,1›, same as the default ease
options.drip: If ‹down›, the whole line drops. On hover the first set stretches vertically up to 2.4x (blur 3.5px · three blood-stain shadows smearing upward) and falls out downward, while the same letters drop in from above and settle. The stretch is a .85s linear keyframe, the move is a .6s linear() curve that briefly pulls up and then slams down, and on leave it is .35s cubic-bezier(.2,1,.3,1) · If ‹up›, it runs in reverse, upward (Brand menu down · footer to-top up). dur · ease · out are accepted as they are.
options.by: With ‹word› the stagger is applied per word instead of per character — spaces are left as they are (Brand button · header link: .02s word interval · .2s · 0.65,0,0.35,1)
options.look: With ‹serif›, only the second copy switches to the title font (--kf-font-display) and aligns to the center of the first copy — the sans-serif letters slide up and out while the same letters rise in as serif (reference menu · back to top: stagger: 0.015; dur: 0.8; ease: 0.215,0.61,0.355,1; gap: 0.1em; look: serif)
options.dir: With ”down” the second copy hides on top of the first and drops down one line to sit in place — the same letters seem to fall from above and swap (Brand menu · View More: stagger: 0; dur: .4; ease: 0.43,0.05,0.17,1; dir: down)
options.outease: Leaving curve in the form ”0.215,0.61,0.355,1” — if omitted, same as ease
options.space: If “skip”, spaces don’t take up a delay slot (only letters are sequenced)
options.lag: The extra wait (seconds) before the first letter starts in mode: hold, default 0 — for when the original starts one cell late with (i+1)× delay (brand .05)

name: char-roll

what: Logo letters over a dark curtain are hidden cell by cell (cell height = line height × 1.5, gap between cells .2 of that). When the typeface arrives the whole block turns on over .9s power2.out, and the letters rise from below their cell in .08s steps over .9s power3.out. Until the document and images have all arrived plus 2 seconds, each letter is followed by the same letter one cell below, and they roll up one cell at a time in .24s steps over 1.2s power2.inOut — it only stops where a full cycle ends, so the letters never misalign (8 seconds at most, unconditionally). When it stops it fires fx:done, the logo moves to the Hero wordmark position over .6s power2.inOut, and then the curtain lifts over .5s power2.out

options.to: Hero wordmark the logo moves to (css selector) — keep the same letter size. If absent, only the curtain lifts in place
options.min: Minimum visible time (sec), default 2
options.max: Time to stop even if documents are late (sec), default 8
options.intro: Initial rise duration (sec), default .9
options.intro-each: Initial stagger for rising in (sec), default .08
options.move: Duration (s) of the move to the wordmark spot, default .6
options.fade: Overlay lift length (s), default .5
options.row: Cell height multiplier (relative to line height), default 1.5
options.gap: Gap between cells (relative to cell height), default .2
options.[data-fx-part=mark]: Logo letters to roll (children) — can be a group of spans with tight spacing between letters
options.fx:done: Event fired from the overlay when it stops and starts to move on (is-done is also added to the overlay) — hook the hero photo zoom-in, header and title rise here

note: THREE·Matter are loaded first as globals — matter.min.js goes before three-global.js (the window.exports trick). If placed after, the UMD goes into exports instead of window.Matter and the coins don’t appear. The canvas sits at the very back of the panel (z 0) with text above it — dragging picks up a coin when the press on the whole panel touches one, so buttons over text can still be pressed. The original’s path-finding that hops across letters in turn was reduced to a single thrown parabola: if a letter box is on the incoming side (the 4-coin width at the left), it is thrown from a height above that letter, and while flying it passes behind without colliding with letter boxes, colliding only after it has fully dropped below the text line (this prevents hitting a box corner mid-flight and piling up inside an offscreen wall or resting on the letters). A coin that fails to enter the panel within 2 seconds fades out. If a line box is the full panel width, like a justified line, coins can’t fall between words, so solid is attached per word. It runs only while the panel is on screen and the tab is visible

name: contour-blob-gl

what: WebGL layer behind the screen — the noise height map is sliced into 24 thin slabs and stacked (each slab keeps only areas higher than its height) to make gray contour steps, then a shadow sampled offset away from the light and a light-side highlight are added. For the first 3s the camera moves to the path’s 0→2s position, then follows scroll progress between the start and end markers at .075 per frame, descending to the 2→8.9s position — the FOV widens 70→124° as it drops into the steps, a rainbow color tied to layer height (0→2.48) fills in, and edge chromatic aberration widens −.15→−.54. At 10.27s the steps vanish, and when the footer marker enters, a different set of steps on the path at 11→13s turns on. Grain .1, bottom darkening (.5 → 0 until progress 15%). Cursor: a 128-cell fluid velocity map (brush radius .035 of screen, motion ×4.23, .9324 applied twice per frame → half-life about 83ms) lights the layers where it passed (hero .057, footer .07 ×5) and jitters layer edges by .004. The camera pivots toward the cursor around a point 1.196 in front of the screen (follows at .032 and .025 per frame, the angle is the path look, and the difference of the two ×.1 is the tilt). On phones, finger drag changes brightness only, and it is off under reduced motion.

name: dash-column-rise

what: The picture is built as a 3D plate of tens of thousands of short horizontal strokes (280×350 cells) — each cell gets its intensity from brightness · warmth · outline, only cells that pass a 4×4 Bayer threshold light up as strokes of cell width .72, pop forward 10~52 by intensity, and ride a five-step color ladder: base → between base and accent → accent → between accent and text → text. At first they are scattered across a sphere of radius 235~365, then gather into the first picture, when the picture changes, each stroke gets its own delay (seed×.45) and flies sideways, bending 18~60 (front-back 46~90) over 1.15s power2.inOut to settle in its new place. The plate tilts .12rad and sways by sin(.32t)×.2, rotates when dragged (easing off at 2.6/s on release, with the tilt returning over .9s power2.out), and the wheel rotates it too. When the mouse moves fast, strokes within 120px are pushed away by (8~22)px (at a speed of 700px/s, 63% of .8, rising at 18/s · falling at 5/s)

what: A WebGL 3D plate that pushes a single photo forward by its depth map on a 128×128 plate (field of view 19° · camera 2.65) — it slowly turns following the mouse up to .17 horizontally · .09 vertically rad (3% of the remaining distance per frame), sways as if breathing at .5 speed even when still, and on hover the upper-left light, matched to normals made from the depth gradient, turns on 8% per frame. Given a lens mask and a reflection video, it reflects the video only on the lens area — compressing plate UV to 2.35x · vertical .54 and raising it by −.67, then reading it bent by fisheye (3.45), lowering color to saturation .75 · brightness .6 at 1.3x strength, and adding a CRT texture of vertical RGB grid 6px and horizontal scanlines 5px. With lit, when the plate turns, the normals turn toward or away from the front light (−3.3 · −4.2 · 4) and the back light, changing the whole plate brightness

The down type is a drawer: the bottom edge of a mask attached to the top droops down round from the center and covers the panel (1s power2.inOut, corners .1s late, and it retracts in the same shape via fx:close). The box type is a center box of 48%×72% whose four edges swell outward and spread to the full screen (2s power3.inOut), which is where the first video grows.

what: The pupil inside the white of the eye looks toward the cursor from anywhere on screen — it travels the eye radius minus the pupil radius and 12px, but when the cursor is within 120px the travel scales down in proportion to the distance (.25s power2.out). When the cursor leaves the window it returns to center in .35s. So small eyes where the pupil nearly fills the white do not move. · The ”spring” type has several eyes on one panel — the cursor position inside the panel (±.5 from center) times 48 moves the pupil layer as a % of its own size, following with a wobble of spring .03, damping .93 and a max of 2.4% per frame. On touch devices it looks only up and down (±100%) based on where the panel passes through the screen. · The ”glance” type has the two pupils of a face drawing aiming at the cursor in steps every 140ms (5 horizontal and 3 vertical units, less within 300px), following in jerks by .45 per frame, and on phones it looks in a random direction every .6 to 1.8 seconds.

name: fade-cycle

what: A single image floats on the display panel and fades out every 4 seconds over .7s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1). Once fully off, it switches to the next image and fades in on the same curve (it also fades in over .7s on first open). Clicking an image enters view mode: the rotation stops and data-viewer is set on the panel, where clicking the left half goes to the previous image and the right half to the next, instantly. Left and right arrow keys, a swipe over 50px and clicking a dot also switch instantly, and leaving with Esc or the close button resumes the 4-second rotation.

options.fade: Off/on duration (s), default .7 — 0 switches instantly
options.[data-fx-part=stage]: (If present) pressable image cell — if none, the whole attached element
options.[data-fx-part=item]: One picture — name in data-title
options.[data-fx-part=title]: (If present) Slot for the current artwork name
options.[data-fx-part=dots]: (optional) slot where dot buttons are created, one per image
options.[data-fx-part=close]: (If any) Button that closes view mode
options.--fx-dot: Dot color of other images (.5 transparent), default --kf-accent

events.fx:change: When the image changes — detail { index, item }
events.fx:viewer: When opening and closing view mode — detail { open, index }

what: A full-panel 3D shape (the default is a hand built from primitive shapes) is rendered separately, and each 12px cell is stamped by brightness with one of five glyphs (cross, empty square, circle, pink cell, purple cell), rotating at .65 rad per second. Where the mouse passes, it spreads as fluid on a grid of 1/8 screen width (fading by .955 and .9 each step), and only that area is re-covered with glyphs while a white wireframe shows through. 450 pin-shaped dust particles flow in from z −12 to 12, and the whole scene gets a threshold 1 bloom (5 levels) and a 10-sample spectral chromatic aberration (1.1 + kick × 8 + (speed − 1) × .45). Holding down builds speed by .02~.6 per frame up to 20x (smoothDamp 1s · max 5/s), and releasing returns it to 1x. On enter (fx:enter), the camera approaches from 50 behind in 2s sine.out, and the dust and trails open in 3s power1.inOut.

what: The plate is tilted −10° and split into 11×22px cells. On every second row, a run of characters (20~50 on wide screens, 10~30 on narrow) is laid at a random horizontal spot — runs switch on one after another at 50ms intervals, and the characters inside a run also switch on at 50ms intervals, cycling through four letters (ACGT) by .2 per tick and stopping at 50 ticks. name: held-zoom-parallax

what: Hangs artwork panels (1.7×1, 8×8 cells) on a cylindrical spiral (three.js, fov 35°, 45° below 900, camera z 8). Panel i stands at position b, which is (i − rolled amount) wrapped by the panel count, at height b×.5 − .8, angle b×.85rad, radius 2, facing outward. Panels bend horizontally on a sin curve (.2), shift right by y²×.1 toward the top and bottom of the screen so the spiral arcs like a bow, and stretch sideways by rolling speed × 2. Each wheel px adds 1.5e-4 (±2 cap) to the target, which is followed .1 per frame and damped by .9 but never drops below .002, so it always turns slowly. A hovered panel (front face only) darkens by .55 and pulls forward 5%, while the back is a blurred image. At the start the panels descend from above at half radius, growing with rounded corners four at a time, staggered 50ms (per frame 1−.95^(dt×.15)). The top and bottom 20% bands of the screen fade into the edge color

what: Draws a rounded-square app icon with a single WebGL2 shader. name: line-redraw-hover

what: Text hides beneath its own line mask, then when it enters the screen each line rises from below (70%) in .5 seconds at .1 second intervals (once only). With split: none the lines are not split and the text rises as one block of children. Distance, length, interval and curve are options — Brand A uses 110% at 1.5 beats, Brand B’s hero words use 105% with a slight overshoot over 1.05 seconds, Brand C’s intro text uses 102% over 1.4 seconds expo.out, and Brand D uses 115% tilted 3° with blur over 1.05 seconds power3.out at .08 second intervals.

options.split: lines (default) — split by line · words — split by word · none — child block as a whole · chars — per character inside a line mask (Brand wordmark)
options.y: Rise distance (%), default 70 — when given, uses only a cover panel with no blur
options.ease: Curve — GSAP name or 0.16,1,0.3,1, default power2.inOut
options.delay: Delay (s)
options.rotate: Tilt (degrees) that unwinds as it rises, default 0 — rotates around the top left of the row
options.fade: “true” makes it light up together from blur (0) even when y is given (default: with y, only via the mask)
options.toggle: If true, not just once — when you scroll back above the trigger position it plays back in reverse (from the last chunk), like the footer wordmark each time you go back and forth
options.fit: Reference font size (px) for stretching the length by text size — if given, the length = dur × (glyph px ÷ fit)^0.2. The bigger the title, the slower it rises (Brand 14)
options.blur: Blur that clears while rising (px), default 0 — reference value 12
options.mask: 「none」 means words and lines rise visible without a cover (Brand site — the default is with a cover)
options.widen: Starting horizontal multiplier that shrinks as it rises, default 1 — corner-panel-stack-studio page large title 1.12 (the start of the text is the axis)
options.tilt: Tilt where the front of the line leans down (rotateX degrees). It rises in perspective (default 600px) and stands at 0. Default 0 · brand −45
options.origin: Rotation pivot for rotate (transform-origin), default “top left” — the ride-plus-a Hero text uses “50% 50%” (center of the text)
options.squash: Initial vertical multiplier that unfolds while rising, default 1 — brand .85 (axis is origin, default top left)
options.jitter: Each row unwinds from a random tilt within ± this angle (deg) to 0, default 0 — Brand 2
options.skew: Angle at which it rises tilted (skewY degrees), default 0 — Brand word 10. The axis is the center (if origin is given, that is used)

name: liquid-arc-carousel

what: A black liquid spreads behind the screen — in a feedback buffer that reads and rewrites the previous frame, while the cursor moves (until 50ms after it stops) a brush stroke of radius .08~.12 (share of screen height) is painted along the path just traveled, flowed by a noise angle field at height 1.85px per step and dried at .95 per second (fixed 1/120s steps, at most 4 steps per frame). The visible screen is dressed from the height field gradient with back light .3, reflection to the 20th power .5 and a rainbow edge rim, with grain dither .1 subtracted, and the background is a round glow bright at the center (.7× brightness). At first a noise blob (radius 1.3) blooms at the center and shrinks over 3s expo.inOut. Press and hold an empty spot for 1s (power2.inOut) and the moment it passes .75 the plate flips so the background darkens, the rainbow rim spreads across the whole liquid, and a .85s power3.out glitch (horizontal slice shifts and color offsets) runs once — release early and it returns, hold again and it comes back from below .25. [data-fx-part=target] When the cursor is over a row, liquid spreads sideways from the cursor spot to fill that row’s box (the box grows over 2.6s from a cursor-height band and gathers into a band at the bottom 30% of the row at 1.1s, all in one expo.out). When it leaves the row, it dries twice as fast over 1s. Sending fx:shock makes a shockwave ring that splits along the grain from that spot (1.5s power3.out, width .07) and spreads to the screen edge, pushing the liquid and darkening and bending the ring area

what: A turbulent pattern in a four-color palette slowly melts and flows inside a large logo/wordmark shape (svg) in WebGL2. The pattern bakes along the shape’s depth (distance from the edge inward) and the edges are bright, so it looks like glass. When the cursor passes, its velocity is stacked into a half-resolution push field with an elliptical brush (radius .09, stretched in the direction of movement) that pushes the pattern. Each frame the field blends .12 with its neighbors and decays by a factor of .895

use: — The shape sits inside the cell, scaled to fit (contain)
note: The depth of the shape is measured at attach time as a 3-4 erosion distance on a buffer and spread over a 6-cell radius (the original uses a design-tool height map). The palette is a straight OKLab mix (the original mixes on an LCH color wheel — with same-family colors the difference is almost nil). The starting phase of the turbulence is a fixed value different from the original random seed (0), so the pattern has the same grain but is not identical. Without a float buffer (EXT_color_buffer_float) there is only flow with no cursor push, and without WebGL2 the shape stays in the accent color. With reduced motion, only one still frame is drawn.

name: luma-threshold-video

what: Dozens of work photo sheets (repeated to reach 30 or more) are lined up in one row like book pages and viewed obliquely from above by an orthographic camera — forming a band that crosses the screen diagonally. One wheel gesture advances one sheet (snapping to the next .15s after release), following eases 4.7% per frame, the advance speed decays ×.829 per frame, and the sheets bend in a sine wave in proportion to that speed. The center sheet pushes its neighbors 4 slots away and rotates (.067, −.363, −.513) rad to face the camera. A hovered side sheet lifts .25 and the center sheet’s photo is pulled in 15.6% (1s power4.out). On entry, 24 sheets flow in with a 2s quartic ease-out and bend heavily, then 1.06s later the center opens (1.1s power2.out).

options.size: Section width, height (scene units), default 4.4,3.5
options.gap: Number of cells the center section pushes neighbors aside, default 4
options.focus: Rotation of the middle sheet in x, y, z (rad), default .06681,-.36331,-.51318
options.follow: Follow share per frame, default .047
options.decay: Remaining speed share per frame, default .829
options.zoom: Orthographic view height (scene units), default 10.8 — smaller means bigger sections
options.min: Minimum number of sheets to repeat-fill, default 30
options.intro: If off, it stops immediately without drifting off
options.on: If manual, it enters when the consumer sends fx:play to the element (after the loader)
options.[data-fx-part=card]: One section — inside (same source) or note in data-label what the photo is (if absent, a skin-colored placeholder picture)
options.fx:center: When the middle section changes { index, count } — Hang info cards, numbers and color swatches here
options.fx:progress: While flipping, every frame { value (0 to section count, decimals allowed), count } — when the side list flows like the band
options.fx:pick: When you tap the center card { index } — Page transition to the detail page goes here (pressing a neighboring slide brings it to the center)
options.fx:step: Sent to the element, it advances by the detail field (default 1) — arrow buttons, keyboard

name: marker-shuffle-chars

what: Hovering a button or link draws two highlighter strokes. The upper stroke goes left to right in .16s power4.out, and the lower stroke goes right to left .048s later. Each stroke is an SVG line (thickness height/2×1.42, slightly tilted) with a segment shown by gradient stops, so the faster the ends, the fainter they are (motion between frames ×2.2, max .3). Only the letters the stroke head has passed switch to the inverted color (upper half and lower half use separate clip-path polygons, including the length where the stroke extends beyond the element, to track progress). name: mask-cycle-slides

what: Photo slides are swapped in WebGL. On open, wait .5s, then a capsule (463:320 superellipse) grows from the center to cover the screen over 1s expo.inOut. From its 1/4 point the first photo is warped like a lens (strength 6 → 0, 1.6s quint.out), held pulled in at .5x, then released over 1.5s quart.out. Every 4 seconds the next photo comes in overlapping for 1.2s sine.inOut with the same warp (1.6s quint.out) and pull (1.5s cubic.out). During each photo’s 5.2s stay it moves closer by 20% (4% on phone), and by a further 40% with the scroll passing through the designated section.
ease: expo.inOut (capsule) · quint.out (bend) · cubic.out / quart.out (pull) · sine.inOut (overlap) · none (hold zoom)

options.fade: Overlap length, default 1.2
options.pull: Pull release length, default 1.5
options.narrow: Narrow screen breakpoint (px), default 1024
options.scroll: CSS for the section that measures scroll zoom (0 when the top touches the screen top → 1 when the bottom passes)
options.mask: If none, goes straight in without the capsule opening
options.mask-warp-at: Initial bend start (capsule length multiples), default .25
options.wait: Wait before opening (s), default .5
options.[data-fx-part=slide]: A single photo — inner Fill it by covering, and if absent draw a placeholder board from the inner .wf-img color and data-label
options.Event fx:mask-distort-slides: detail.index from the element — each time it moves on to the next photo

options.cover: Time (s) for the curtain to cover after a link is clicked, default 0.35 — the next page is only called once fully covered, so navigation is delayed by this much
options.reveal: Seconds for the cover to lift on an opened page, default 0.45 — starts .05s later and is fully visible at .05 + reveal seconds (default .5s)

options.ease: Curve — both cover and reveal use this (GSAP name or ”0.16,1,0.3,1”). Default cover power2.in · reveal power2.out
options.delay: Delay (seconds) before the cover lifts on an opened page, default 0.05
options.look: split — two sheets, top and bottom (contrast stage color), close and open (Brand A type) · centre — a single background-color sheet opens from the center vertical line to both sides and covers (Brand B: cover default .9 · power3.inOut, on the opened page reveal default 0 — visible right away). rise — a single accent-color sheet rises with the bottom edge as the axis to cover (scaleY 0→1) and on the opened page lifts away with the top edge as the axis (Brand C: cover and lift .6 · power3.inOut · wait 0). If not set, a single background-color sheet fades in to cover · layers — a curtain of three overlapping sheets: accent, light accent and contrast stage colors. On press they unfold from the bottom sheet at .05s intervals with the left edge as the axis to cover, and on the opened page they fold left from the top sheet at .05s intervals to lift away (Brand D: cover and lift .6 · power3.inOut · wait 0). On phones (768 and below) it uses scaleY, with .1s intervals when covering. The three sheet colors are --fx-layer-1·2·3 (style) · slide — a single background-color sheet pushes up from below to cover (translateY 100%→0) and on the opened page slides straight up and away (Brand E: cover and lift 1 · cubic-bezier(.64,.04,.35,1) · wait 0) · circle — an accent-color curtain covers as a circle from one corner (at) over .7s expo.inOut, with the mark turning in at −90° and .7x (after .35s, .5s expo.out). On the opened page the mark disappears in .25s and the circle shrinks to the opposite corner (to) over .8s (after .15s — Brand F)
options.stagger: look: split — gap in seconds between the two sheets, default cover .04 · uncover .03 · look: layers — gap between sheets (default .05, phone cover .1)
options.wait: With load, the open page’s curtain is lifted after window load (fonts·images too) — for when a white curtain acts as the loading screen without a loader, like the original site. Otherwise it lifts immediately when the script runs.
options.reveal-ease: Curve for only the reveal on the opened page (GSAP name or ”0.16,1,0.3,1”) — if empty, it follows ease. Brand: cover expo.inOut · reveal power4.out
options.at · to: look: circle covering corner · revealing corner (clip-path coordinates), default ‹100% 0%› · ‹0% 100%›

name: page-veil

what: When moving to another document on the same site, a browser View Transition is used — the old screen shrinks to .9× in place and fades to .25, while the new screen opens over it with a clip-path from bottom to top. Both run 1.75s cubic-bezier(.86,0,.07,1). Ordinary links that load a new document work as they are, so page scripts need not be split

options.dur: Transition length (s), default 1.75 — shorten it if pages change often, like in an app
options.shrink: Scale the old screen shrinks to, default .9
options.fade: End opacity as the old screen fades, default .25
options.ease: Curve (”.86,0,.07,1” or a css curve name), default cubic-bezier(.86,0,.07,1)
options.shift: Distance the old screen travels down while shrinking (measured after shrinking, px if no unit), default 0 — brand 5vw
options.origin: Axis on which the old screen shrinks, default center · ‹top› means top-edge center — brand top
options.clip: The share of the new screen covered from the top at the start (inset top), default 100% (fully covered). brand 85vh (starts with only the bottom 15% visible)
options.rise: Distance the new screen is initially pushed down, default 0 — Brand page 15vh

use: <html data-fx="page-vt-reveal"> — On both pages involved in the transition. Load fx.css in the head (@view-transition can only be enabled from css)
note: Cross-document View Transition (same origin) in Chrome 126+ and Safari 18.2+. Where View Transition does not work, such as a page opened from a file, only the body of the page reached by a link opens from below with the same curve (no old-screen shrink). The original is a single-page app (next-view-transitions), so it runs the same keyframes within one document.

name: page-vt-reveal

what: Pressing the MENU button makes paint drip down from the top of the screen to cover it. There is one stream every 70px of screen width, and each line flows an extra 0 to 30px by simplex noise (x is line index × .15, time in 1.2s units), so the lower edge undulates and joins in rounded curves. It starts slow at 3 × .25 px per frame, speeds up with (progress^.5) to as much as 7x as it goes down, and the undulation grows to 1.6x. The streams stop 40px above the bottom of the screen and keep undulating while covering (unlike the original, it does not move on to a “fully open” state). Pressing again hides the menu panel immediately, and the paint retracts upward at 30px per frame. The color is one of three skin colors, chosen each time it opens

options.[data-fx-part=panel]: Menu panel that shows instantly on open and hides instantly on close (optional)
options.[data-fx-part=close]: Close buttons and links inside the panel (optional, multiple)
options.[data-fx-part=canvas]: Canvas to paint on (optional, created if missing)
options.colors: Skin variable names (comma-separated), default --kf-accent, --kf-accent-soft, --kf-warning — brand uses --site-green, --site-purple, --site-yellow
options.dist: Water stream spacing (px), default 70
options.back: Collecting speed (px/frame), default 30 — never pass 0 or the panel breaks
options.below: Extra distance scrolled below the screen (px), default 40
options.over: Past this distance it fills with one color and stops (px), default 150 — if larger than below, it does not pass through and keeps swaying (same as the original)

name: pill-window-flow

what: Draws a column of photo panels stacked seamlessly, alternating portrait and landscape, in WebGL, and spins it endlessly with wheel, drag and arrow keys. Wheel adds delta × .03 to velocity, damped by .97 per frame (.92 on phones). .5s after release (1s after drag), the panel nearest the 25% screen spot in the travel direction snaps to center over .8s power2.out. The image inside each panel shifts up and down the farther it is from center (distance relative to screen width × .6). At first the panels overlap at center as 8px dots, spread from .5s into a single line at 32px spacing (1.75s), fade from black into the picture (2s), and from 2s over 2.5s stand up into the full-size column (power3.inOut). Side list names change opacity .15–.95 by circular distance from the center panel (1s power3.out), and clicking a name goes to that panel. Pressing the landscape button restacks the panels into a double-size horizontal strip over 1.5s, starting with those farthest from center at .06s steps

what: While the long section is pinned, as scroll progresses 1650 dots (phone 900) light up layer by layer from the inside out to form a cloud. Each dot has its own turn-on share (.035~.6) and grows (.72 → 1.18x) as it appears between that share −.035 and +.075, and the first 26 are seeds that are lit from the start. what: 44,000 dots pinned behind the screen (22,000 on touch devices) return from a scattered starfield (radius 2~6.5) over 2.8s, each delayed 0~.55 with cubic out (1.4rad swirl), and settle into an upper-body figure attached to the bottom of the screen (90% height). With each scroll screen they morph via smoothstep into a globe (evenly spread sphere, radius height×.42, .06 turns per second), a map (a slanted peninsula), and a double helix (rungs 1/6, rotating .6rad per second, strands roughening with scroll speed). The camera sits at height 6.4 with a 32° field of view, shifts .2 toward the cursor and looks .28 that way (.85s power3.out). Hovering a card lifts it slightly over .4s thomas(.625,.05,0,1). Picking it up raises it .3 so it follows the hand (response 11.5) and tilts with the drag speed. what: A dial that turns a one-screen stage with wheel, drag and arrow keys to pick items one at a time. note: The original uses framer-motion (drag, dragSnapToOrigin, dragTransition bounceStiffness 600 and bounceDamping 20, whileHover 1.075, whileTap 1.05, whileDrag rotate 10 scale 1.05). Curves were matched by measuring the original with motion-probe — transitions given only a duration (hover .1s, phone fade-out .1s) use easeOut(0,0,.58,1), and the blur given only a delay uses framer’s default opacity curve (.3s, .25,.1,.35,1). Like framer, pick and hover update the indicator (--fx-focus, --fx-hover) before anything moves, and picking happens on the click event that follows pointerup, not on pointerup itself (same timing as framer onClick). The drag threshold is the same 3px as framer — release after moving less than that and it counts as a press. While picked, drag and press are off, and even after picking, the hover scale on the drag shell stays until the hand leaves (as in the original). The caller listens for fx:focus, fx:press, fx:grab and fx:drop to attach the description panel, the left and right buttons and the sound effects. Drag works on devices without hover too (touch-action: none only on the sticker) — pushing outside the panel scrolls the page. To use GSAP like framer, the caller sets gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(40, 40) (caps one frame of progress at 40ms) (Brand shared.js). The name pill stands at 85% up the box (anchor) of the pre-shrink image size — floating above the sticker like the original.

The default (fade) is opacity 0→1 over 1.2s on a curve that brightens quickly at first and settles slowly. pop is scale 0→1 over .45s, popping out .1s late and settling after a slight overshoot (illustrations, speech bubbles). grow is vertical scale 0→1 and opacity 0→1 around a bottom-center axis over .3s cubic-bezier(.4,.4,0,1) (a new site builder version — a character peeking up over the footer). left slides in from 50px to the left over .6s ease-in-out while brightening (big hero text), and right comes in from 40px to the right over .8s with a .4s delay (side-by-side videos and cards). up floats up from 20px below over .8s with the default CSS ease while brightening (the site builder’s common fade up — the delay is often .3s and headline lines use 1.3s). settle lands a panel from 1.05× scale and angular corners to its own size and corners over .8s cubic-bezier(.4,.4,0,1), and zoom resolves from 1.05× scale and transparent over the same length (hero panel and the photo inside it). blur resolves a panel from 50px blur over 1.2s cubic-bezier(.4,.4,0,1) (opacity unchanged — a frosted glass panel). haze resolves from 10px blur and transparent (with a --fx-y shift) over 2s ease-out (the site builder’s &appear{filter: blur(10px); opacity: 0} — text and vertical titles rising out of mist) tilt starts transparent, offset (-25px, 24px) and rotated -15°, and drops into place over .6s (wall-hung tool and prop pictures — direction changed with --fx-x·--fx-y·--fx-rotate). gray returns its color from 68% grayscale over 1.4s (photos — setting --fx-o to 0 brightens them together from transparent). skew settles at a slant over 1s cubic-bezier(.45,0,.55,1) from a spot that is transparent, blurred 4px, skew(-2°,-2°), offset (-20,-20)px (STUDIO .appear{filter: blur(4px); what: Each panel gets only a long scroll stretch while the visible stage stays pinned to the screen and overlaps the others. When a panel’s top touches the top of the screen, the stage that was on scales up to 1.05 and turns off over .5s, then the new stage turns on from 1.05 → 1 over .5s (power1.out). If the body text is taller than the window inside the stage, the stretch grows by that much. While scrolling through the middle of the stretch, the text flows upward inside the window with the top and bottom 10% faded by a mask (scrub). Scrolling back above the first panel or past the last panel turns the stage off.

options.dur: Length of each off and on phase (sec), default .5

options.--fx-panel-h: Scroll length of one section (css), default 200svh — never shorter than the screen height
options.--fx-window-gap: Window height = Screen height minus this value (css), default 40svh

name: swap-tint-cycle

what: A board of staggered-height photo columns flows left and right following the horizontal mouse position (overflow width × ratio, .05 per frame, returns to center when the cursor leaves). Rolling the wheel makes each column follow deltaY/2 with a different duration (.5/.8/.2/.3/.6s power3), so they stagger (up to half the column height). After 3 seconds idle at the top, the columns sink 70px one by one (1s power1.inOut, photo turns off at .9s), swap the first photo for the next, and rise back (turns on at .85s, cell background changes to the new photo’s dominant color in .5s) — .62s between columns, 3s rest after a full round. While it runs window.lenis is paused, and if the wheel was rolled in the meantime it stops at the end of the round

options.lerp: Rate at which the panel follows the mouse (per frame), default .05
options.min: Minimum window width (px) at which the panel follows the mouse, default 992
options.lags: Duration each column follows the wheel (seconds, comma-separated), default .5,.8,.2,.3,.6
options.wheel: Column shift per 1px of wheel, default .5
options.idle: Seconds until the wheel starts turning at the top, default 3
options.rest: Pause after one loop (sec), default 3
options.wait: If event, hand reactions and the spin stay paused until the host fires an fx:start event on the panel (starts after the intro)
options.[data-fx-part=track]: Panel with overflowing width (required) — flows with the mouse
options.[data-fx-part=col]: Pillar (must exist) — rises with the wheel. A hidden pillar (display:none) is dropped from the wheel
options.[data-fx-part=media]: Photo cell inside the pillar — the first two sink. Receives the data-tint of the swapped photo
options.[data-fx-part=next]: Next photos hidden at the end of the column — they enter the first cell in turn and the photo that leaves goes back to the end. With data-tint, the cell background takes that color

what: Clicking a link to another page makes a light panel fill from the bottom of the screen upward and cover it — five layers of noise are added to the horizontal edge before the threshold so the edge tears off in pieces rather than waves, and torn-off fragments float ahead. It covers in .52s and transitions, then on the arriving page it clears toward the same upward direction starting at the 36% point of a 1.4s length (flipping only the opaque side for one continuous directional motion). The curve is a first-order filter with a time constant of .5s (fast at first, soft at the end). The panel is a gradient from #efefef at the top → a lighter color below (skin variable). WebGL shader

options.cover: Cover duration (s), default .52
options.clear: Walk length (seconds), default 1.4 — the leading skip share is skipped
options.skip: Skip the first part of the walk (0~1), default .36 — dead time where the panel sits still because the edge is still off screen
options.amp: How strongly noise pulls the boundary (share of screen height), default .175
options.reach: Multiplier applied to amp, default 2.7 — page-turn·loader panels tear more than the tear between blocks
options.scale: Noise scale, default 3 — larger means finer fragments
options.detail: Noise layer count (1~6), default 5 — 1 is smooth waves, 5 is fragments
options.soft: Edge half-width, default .001 — smaller makes the shards crisper
options.dir: up (default, bottom to top) · down
options.nav: when off, links are not intercepted — from a transition tool such as barba, fire an fx:tear event (on root{ phase: 'cover'|'clear', done }sends ) to use it
options.--fx-sheet-top · --fx-sheet-foot: Colors above and below the panel: the default --kf-contrast-bg and a slightly lighter one. To cover briefly with another color like a loader, set a class on html and change the two variables of .fx-tear (re-read on every turn)
options.[data-fx-part=hide]: Child that hides at .2s while the panel is present

what: Text starts with !=*+/?<>Scrambled with %#&@ and digits, then once visible it resolves into the right letters one by one from the front over 1.4s (the remaining part reshuffles every frame) · with speed it sweeps from the left edge in px per second while resolving (450px/s on one site), and look: dim makes the letters faint before they resolve · with repeat it rests that long after fully resolving, then scrambles and resolves again (2s on one site) · order: random makes each letter resolve by chance, flickering here and there before settling (.5s on another)

options.chars: Scramble character set, default !=*+/?<>%#&@0123456789 — Name is A!B@C#D$E%F&G*H?J[K]L{M}N=O+P-QRSTUVWXYZ
options.on: scroll (default — when visible) · load (right on load, after delay) · hover (shows its own text at first, and scrambles then resolves only on hover — signal-a footer link) · manual (does not start by itself, only when fx:play is sent — the menu drawer rewritten each time it opens)
options.delay: Seconds to wait before the first write begins (load, scroll and fx:play alike), default 0
options.each: In the life type, the per-letter stagger in seconds — when set, the total length follows the text length as life + each×(letter count − 1) instead of duration. The band site (shuffleLetters 20fps, 2-letter window) uses life: .1; each: .05
options.fx:play: Send this event to an element and it rewrites from the initial form (lead: blank means empty) after the delay
options.hold: Share held fully mixed (0~1), default 0 — then releases from the front
options.speed: If set, instead of letter order it reveals by sweeping from the element’s left edge at speed px per second (multi-line text moves together for the same x) — duration is width/speed. 450 for Brand
options.mix: In width mode, letters are shuffled among same-width groups (i·l, m·w, Hangul syllables for Korean) so line breaks don’t jitter while shuffling · in case mode, uppercase shuffles with A–Z·0–9, lowercase with a–z·0–9, and any other character with letters (the character classes of shuffleLetters)
options.flicker: Interval (seconds) for re-shuffling the mixed side, default 0 (every frame) — brand uses .03
options.look: If dim, the mixed side fades to 30% of the text color (Brand’s light-gray text before decoding)
options.fade: when on, the whole text opacity also fades up from 0 → 1 while mixing (brand)
options.repeat: Interval in seconds to rest as the original text after fully resolving, then scramble-resolve again, default 0 (once) — Brand corner text uses 2
options.order: With random, instead of resolving from the front, each character at each frame shows its final letter with a probability equal to the progress (all mixed → patchy → all resolved) — a reference site uses duration: .5; chars: ABSDabsd0123456789; order: random; start: top bottom
options.life: Blend time per letter (seconds) — if given, each letter blends and resolves in order from the front (stagger gap = (duration − life)/(letter count − 1)). signal-a has duration: .4; life: .06; flicker: .02
options.lead: If blank, letters before their turn are empty (they’re written mixing in from blanks — signal-a)
options.hover: If on, it reshuffles and resolves again without blanks each time the pointer hovers (signal-a menu · Work titles)
options.steps: Text is written in chunks of N characters from the start — for each chunk, only those N characters scramble for duration ÷ number of chunks while the rest stays empty. Default 0 (none) · david-brand banner steps: 2; duration: .6, About text steps: 3; duration: .7, tech title steps: 1; duration: .35 — chars: ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789
options.idle: If full, before writing it hides itself transparently with all its characters already in place (keeping space and height), then clears and turns on when it starts. The clearing happens one step (each) before the delay. Sending fx:rest returns it to that resting state (when the menu closes). Brand site .typewrite·.typewrite-menu
options.fx:rest: idle: stops what was used in full and returns to its own letters·transparent
options.space: If skip, blanks don’t take a turn (life type — only the letters go in order, like shuffleLetters)
options.jitter: In the life type, a random 0 to jitter seconds is added to each letter’s turn, default 0 — Brand work titles use each: .036; life: .072; jitter: .028

what: Tens of thousands of small poster cells running endlessly across the full screen are split and drawn with a WebGL2 weighted Voronoi, with a fisheye lens in the center — inside the lens cells are enlarged 15x in their original color, the edge is thin bands squeezed toward the diameter, outside the lens is dimmed in two grayscale tones, and a ripple (frequency 30 · speed 2 · strength .02) runs. Cell positions are grid plus jitter and are re-placed every frame by forces (pull to grid .8 · focus pushes neighbors away .3 · velocity damping .7, alpha .2). The board is pushed by as much as the cursor moves (follow .15 · max 10px/frame) so different cells pass under the lens, and the cell at the lens center becomes the focus, gaining weight and growing. If the cursor jumps (frame movement over 7 times the recent 10-frame average (min 2px)), changes direction three times within 250ms, or leaves the board, the cursor is frozen and the board stops, and it reattaches only when the cursor returns slowly, under 5px/frame on average, within 50px of the frozen spot. Wheel up · press gives the pick view (lens 1.9x · speed 4 · follow .1), wheel down · press · Esc returns, and arrow keys move one cell at a time. In the intro the large cells (11x) recede to 1x over 3.2s, then the lens swells over 1s

what: Behind the plate sits a wave terrain drawn with bold grid lines (44 cells, line width about 1.6px on screen). A 2×2 plane split into 160 segments heaves up and down by noise height (amplitude .5, frequency 1.6) and drifts slowly with time × .1. The plane lies tilted at 15° (X) and 45° (Y), scaled up 10.6 times, and fades with distance (z 6~32). what: Columns of equal height (number, photo, year, description) stand side by side. They chase the distance received from wheel or drag by 7.5% per frame at 60fps, and a column that leaves the screen wraps to the opposite side by the full row width so the strip loops endlessly. On release, it glides a further last velocity × 500. Pressing a column brings only that column to the center and expands it to the open width (probe width, or 70% of the screen, 90% on phones) over .75s expo.out, pushing the columns on its right by the added amount. While one is open, the wheel does not move the row. Esc, an outside press or the close button folds it back over .75s cubic-bezier(.5,0,0,1) keeping the center, and pressing ← or → while open folds it and then opens the neighboring column. While moving, the board gets is-fx-moving (used to turn hover off), on-screen columns get is-fx-inview, and the open column gets is-fx-open

About
note: A ”large board explorer” like drag-pan-map (Draggable · InertiaPlugin inertia), but with wheel push, zoom and table-of-contents fly-to added, and inertia based on a velocity decay formula, so it is kept separate. Dragging the board is this part’s job, so touch on the board is blocked — a board covering the full window height would stop the page from scrolling on that screen, so attach it only when the board is used as the whole page (the entire first screen). · FOCAL: the original zooms from the window center using the page’s top-left as the reference point, but this part uses the board center as the reference, so positions drift a little differently during zoom.
